ca_witch_the.blurb: The Witch is one of the granite spires strung along the Needles ridge high above the Kern River in the southern Sierra. All 21 routes here are traditional, and they are mostly long, steep crack lines on clean, sound rock. Grades cluster in the 5.10 range, with a few 5.9 outings to start on and a handful of 5.11 and 5.12 leads for strong parties. Many of the area's best-loved lines sit in the amphitheater between this spire and its neighbor, so expect multi-pitch days with a full rack. The setting is remote and quiet compared with most Sierra destinations, and summers can run hot despite the elevation.

ca_trashcan_rock_west_face.blurb: The west face of Trashcan Rock is a friendly little wall in the northwest part of Joshua Tree National Park, right beside the Quail Springs picnic area. Nearly all of its 21 routes are single-pitch trad, with one top-rope line. The range is wide: several routes are scrambly and very easy, a solid group sits between 5.6 and 5.9, and a few harder leads reach into the low 5.11s. That mix makes it a common first stop for newer climbers, and because some of the lines are poorly protected, top-roping is popular. Expect plenty of ropes and beginner groups, especially on weekends.
ca_trashcan_rock_west_face.parking_note: Leave the car in the paved Quail Springs picnic area lot, on the right roughly six miles after the West (Joshua Tree) entrance. The rock stands only a few steps from the pavement.

ca_balconies_the.blurb: The Balconies is a cliff on the west side of Pinnacles National Park, a short hike up the trail from the west-side parking. The climbing is a blend of multi-pitch trad, bolted sport lines and a single aid route, with most of the 21 routes falling between 5.8 and 5.11 and a few easier and harder ones around the edges. The volcanic rock is softer than granite, so test holds, wear a helmet and expect an adventurous feel; many older bolts have been replaced with modern hardware and much of the loose stone has been cleaned. Pitches are short to moderate and the setting is open and scenic.

ca_d_northwest_recess.blurb: Northwest Recess is the recessed middle section of Tahquitz Rock, the big granite face above the town of Idyllwild in the San Jacinto Mountains. It holds about 20 routes, nearly all traditional and a couple of them among the longest on the rock, running six pitches or more. Grades are weighted toward the upper end of the scale, with a lot of 5.11 alongside a decent selection of 5.8 to 5.10 and a single 5.12. Protection can be sparse on this cliff, and the north side has a reputation for loose rock and falling debris from parties above, so go early, bring a helmet and choose your day carefully.

ca_stumbling_blocks.blurb: Stumbling Blocks is a compact sport crag in Malibu Creek State Park, in the Santa Monica Mountains northwest of Los Angeles. Most of the 21 climbs are short, steep pitches on pocketed volcanic rock, with a couple of top-rope lines and one boulder problem tucked in. Grades run from an easy 5.5 up to the low 5.13s, but the core is 5.10 and 5.11, with a few warm-ups around 5.8 and 5.9. Oak trees shade some of the faces, though the surrounding hillside is dry and open, so carry water. It is one of the park's most popular spots and busy on weekends.

ca_cascade_cliff.blurb: Cascade Cliff is a solid granite wall high on the Tahoe West Shore, near the top of Maggies Peak South with views down to Cascade Lake and Lake Tahoe. It is a hard-climbers' crag: all 21 routes are 5.11 or harder, with the largest group in 5.12 and a few lines reaching 5.14. Most are sport routes, with about a quarter needing gear, so bring a small rack as well as quickdraws. The wall lies in shade by early afternoon in summer. It sits well off the main recreation areas, so it stays isolated and quiet, and the selection is small enough to be worked in a day or two.
